result.topic_en: This page ends a comparison of integral forms for Lagrange's method. It then states the rule that the arbitrary constant be fixed so that x = k when y = 0, and gives Theorem I: the normalized integral of dx/(a+bx+cxx) − dy/(a+by+cyy) = 0.

Ex iis, quae hactenus ſunt allata, ſatis liquet, eandem aequationem integralem innumeris modis exhiberi poſſe, prout conſtans arbitraria alio atque alio modo repraeſentatur; vnde plurimum intererit certam legem ſtabilire, ſecundum quam quouis caſu conſtantem illam arbitrariam exprimere velimus. Hunc in finem iſta regula obſeruetur: vt perpetuo integralia ita capiantur, vt poſito $y=0$ fiat $x=k$, hincque ſecundum legem compoſitionis $X=K$, exiſtente
$K = + A + Bk + Ckk + Dk^3 + Ek^4$
Hac enim lege obſeruata omnia integralia, vtcunque diuerſa videantur, ad perfectum conſenſum perduci poterunt. Hoc igitur modo quae hactenus inuenimus ſequentibus Theorematibus complectamur.

Theorema I.
§. 48. Si haec aequatio differentialis
$\frac{dx}{a+bx+cxx} - \frac{dy}{a+by+cyy} = 0,$
ita integretur, vt poſito $y=0$ fiat $x=k$, integrale ita ſe habebit:
$\frac{2a+b(x+y)+2cxy}{x-y} = \frac{2a+bk}{k}.$

items.english: Meanwhile, however, it is not easily understood how this form agrees with those found before, although we can be certain of the agreement.

items.quote: Hunc in finem iſta regula obſeruetur: vt perpetuo integralia ita capiantur, vt poſito $y=0$ fiat $x=k$, hincque ſecundum legem compoſitionis $X=K$
items.english: To this end let this rule be observed: the integrals are always to be taken so that, when y = 0, x = k, and hence by the law of composition X = K.

items.quote: Hac enim lege obſeruata omnia integralia, vtcunque diuerſa videantur, ad perfectum conſenſum perduci poterunt.
items.english: With this rule observed, all the integrals, however different they may appear, can be brought into perfect agreement.

items.english: If this differential equation dx/(a+bx+cxx) − dy/(a+by+cyy) = 0 is integrated so that x = k when y = 0, the integral will be (2a+b(x+y)+2cxy)/(x−y) = (2a+bk)/k.
